verdict.rationale_short: (1) ★★ POSITION-CLEARING PHASE — Bloomberg and Tickmill explicitly characterize Friday's semiconductor selloff as having 'graduated from profit-taking to position-clearing,' with leveraged retail AI investors forced to unwind. MSCI Asia Pacific –2.7% (approaching 2-month low); Nikkei 225 –5.2% (steepest decline since March); Taiwan Exchange –6%+ (worst session since Liberation Day tariffs); Kioxia –16%; SoftBank –9%+; TSMC Taipei –7.3%. (2) ★★ PREMARKET ROUT — S&P 500 futures –0.9% (~7,466 — testing the 7,460 support level); Nasdaq 100 futures –1.9%; Dow futures –0.6% (–335 pts). iShares Semiconductor ETF –3.7%; VanEck SMH –3.4%. NVDA –3% premarket (~$201); AMAT –5%; LRCX –5%; ARM –4%; Micron –4%. For the major averages: S&P 500 is down 0.6% for the week; Nasdaq down 1.5%. (3) ★★ BRENT $85.95 — Most acute Hormuz escalation yet. US struck an Iranian oil tanker near Tehran's main oil export terminal (first time since blockade was imposed); Iran retaliated overnight with strikes on US military bases in Kuwait and Jordan. Brent crude +2.04% to $85.95; WTI +1% to $79.74 (on track for >10% weekly gain). Brent at $85.95 is the structural signal that August CPI will embed a material energy-shock component regardless of Friday WTI settlement. (4) ★★ NETFLIX MISS — Q2 slight EPS beat ($0.80 vs $0.79 est) but Q3 guidance missed both lines: revenue guidance $12.86B vs $13.01B est; EPS guidance $0.82 vs $0.84 est. Shares –8.58% AH to $67.97 — 52-week low dating to September 2024. Netflix's guide miss extends the 'sell elevated-multiple consumer tech' dynamic heading into Friday open. (5) ★★ BTC APPROACHING GATE 2 TRIGGER — $62,810 (–1.86% 24h); $810 above the $62,000 Gate 2 defensive protocol trigger established in prior briefings. Cross-asset risk-off alignment: BTC falling while Brent rises = supply shock + risk aversion simultaneously. Gate 2 breach ($62,000 close) activates defensive protocol. (6) ★ CPI/PPI DISINFLATION (priced in July 14) — June core CPI 0.0% MoM (2.6% YoY vs 2.8% prior); PPI –0.3% (steepest wholesale decline since April 2020). Fed July hike probability collapsed from ~46% to ~15-20% on CME FedWatch. September probability reduced but still meaningful given Brent $85.95 loading into August CPI. This is the primary counterpoint that prevents the verdict from upgrading to BEARISH/DEFENSIVE. (7) ★ NVDA CUMULATIVE –10%+ IN TWO SESSIONS — From $212.50 (July 15 close) to $207.40 (July 16 close) to ~$201 premarket July 17 = –5.4% cumulative two-day. Thursday's $195 hard stop held but the second-session decline threatens to re-test it. At $201 (~37x forward earnings), the TSMC wafer hike cost impact is still not fully reflected in sell-side forward EPS models.

Bloomberg, Tickmill, and IG analysts all characterize Friday's Asia rout as a leveraged unwind, not a fundamental re-rate response. In position-clearing phases, the initial selling exhaustion point typically requires a fundamental catalyst (earnings confirmation) to stop — not a single session's bounce. NVDA Q2 FY27 is August 26; the 5-week dead zone means SMH has no upside catalyst to override the structural wafer-hike margin headwind. SMH at premarket –3.4% still has room to fall as US markets open.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: the June CPI (core 0.0% MoM, 2.6% YoY) and PPI (–0.3% MoM) data released July 14 are the most definitive disinflation prints since the Iran-Hormuz conflict began, collapsing Fed July hike probability from 46% to ~15-20%. The market is simultaneously pricing a supply shock (Brent $85.95) and genuine demand-side disinflation — these signals are contradictory, and history suggests oil-shock CPI effects take 90-120 days to embed. The 'position-clearing' narrative is a classic contrarian buy signal: when sell-side desks, Bloomberg, and Tickmill simultaneously describe a selloff as 'position-clearing,' the marginal seller is already in the market. NVDA at $201 — after recovering from $197 to $210 Thursday, now –3% — is still 37x forward earnings on $91B annualized revenue with TSMC supply shortages (N3/N5) confirmed through 2027 by the TSMC call transcript itself. SoftBank and Kioxia selling off in Japan is the most distant read-through to US AI hyperscaler demand; those companies are two removed from NVDA's core revenue driver. If SPX closes above 7,480 today — defending the 7,460 support with a positive weekly close — and VIX stays below 17, the STEP ASIDE call may have caught the panic low. Invalidation: If SPX closes above 7,520 with NVDA above $204 and BTC above $63,500 on Friday, raise the verdict to HOLD/SELECTIVE for Monday.
